options.content:
# ⚡Virtual Machine Power & Carbon Emissions Dashboard Method 2 This dashboard estimates the **power consumption** and **carbon emissions** of an OpenStack Virtual Machine (VM) over a selected time period.
The calculation is based on the VM’s allocated CPU cores and its utilisation relative to the host’s power profile. > ⚠️ The results represent an **approximation**, not an exact measurement of VM energy usage.
> ⚠️ This dashboard supports Compute (CPU) flavours only.
`GPU flavours are not supported and may produce incorrect estimates.` ## 🧭 How to Use This Dashboard 1. **Select your VM Instance Name:**
Use the Instance Name dropdown at the top of the dashboard to select your VM.
2. **Handle duplicate VM names (if applicable):**
-If multiple VMs share the same name:
-Go to: https://openstack.stfc.ac.uk
-Navigate to: Project → Instances
-Find the correct VM and copy its Instance ID (UUID)
-In Grafana, after selecting the instance name, choose the corresponding VM UUID from the UUID variable dropdown
5. **Select the time range:**
Choose the time period you want to analyse using the time picker.
6. **View the Results, the dashboard will display:**
Estimated VM power consumption
Estimated carbon emissions ## 🧮 Calculation Method The VM power consumption is estimated based on:
- How much of the host machine your VM is allocated (CPU cores)
- How actively your VM is using those CPU resources (utilisation)
- How the host server’s power changes between idle and full load
📐 Formula: `Average Watts = Min Watts + Avg vCPU Utilization * (Max Watts - Min Watts)`
Source: https://www.cloudcarbonfootprint.org/docs/methodology
Implemented equation: `VM Power ≈ (VM CPU Cores / Host CPU Cores) × [Host Min Power + VM Utilisation × (Host Max Power − Host Min Power)]`
## ⚠️ Important Limitations The VM power attribution is calculated only from CPU resources and does not include:
- Memory (RAM) usage - Disk storage and I/O activity - Network traffic - GPU or accelerator usage
Workloads that rely heavily on these resources may therefore have their actual energy usage under- or over-estimated.
Therefore, this dashboard currently supports only Compute (CPU) flavours.
GPU flavours are not supported and will not produce accurate power or carbon estimates. ## 🌱 Purpose of This Dashboard: This dashboard helps users: - Understand the energy footprint of their virtual machines. - Estimate carbon emissions of workloads - Support sustainability and energy awareness in using STFC Cloud
